title: Bram and the Ember
premise: Emrys Galloway, an exiled storm-caller hiding in the Thornfell mountains, has spent a decade erasing their own name from every record and memory they could reach. When the old gods stir beneath the mountain and begin answering prayers again, Emrys learns that a desperate village girl, Bram, sold her brother's soul to the court below to survive a plague winter—and the gods now demand payment through her. To save Bram from becoming the court's new vessel, Emrys must descend into the Ember Court, where memories are currency and their own forgotten past waits in the vaults. In the climax, Emrys trades their hard-won invisibility—every erased memory of themselves—for the boy's soul, discovering that the exile they fled was self-inflicted: they once served the gods and burned their own name to escape. The book ends with Emrys remembered by everyone at once, powerless but free, guiding Bram home as the old gods, starved of worship, finally go quiet.
about_author: Sebastian Coldharbour is the pen name of a former alpine guide who claims to have mapped smuggler routes that appear on no official chart. They write fantasy steeped in mountain folklore and insist all their stories were told to them by weather.

chapters.title: The Road That Forgets Itself
chapters.summary: Emrys Galloway guides a salt caravan through a pass that shouldn't exist, demonstrating their talent for moving unseen through Thornfell. When the caravan's dogs refuse to enter a shrine cave, Emrys feels the first tremor of returning divine attention. POV: Emrys. Emotional beat: the uneasy comfort of a life built on being forgotten.

chapters.title: Prayers With Teeth
chapters.summary: In the mining town of Cinderhollow, offerings left at a dead shrine are answered overnight—a drowned child walks out of the river. Emrys recognizes the signature of the Ember Court and knows the old gods have woken. POV: Emrys. Emotional beat: dread disguised as professional curiosity.

chapters.title: The Girl Who Bargained
chapters.summary: Emrys meets Bram, a fourteen-year-old survivor of the plague winter who traded her brother Tam's soul to a voice in the well so her family would be spared. She doesn't understand what she gave away; she only knows Tam stopped dreaming. POV: Bram. Emotional beat: guilt worn as stubbornness.

chapters.title: A Debt Written in Ash
chapters.summary: Emrys examines the contract-mark on Bram's palm and realizes the Ember Court intends to use her body as its vessel when the debt comes due at the solstice. Running is impossible—the mark finds its bearer. POV: Emrys. Emotional beat: reluctant responsibility for a stranger's mistake.

chapters.title: What the Storm Remembers
chapters.summary: Emrys attempts to call a storm to scour the mark away, but the lightning bends toward them, whispering a name they don't recognize: their own. Something in the mountains knows who they used to be. POV: Emrys. Emotional beat: the first crack in a carefully constructed identity.

chapters.title: The Cartographer of Small Mercies
chapters.summary: Emrys seeks out Vess, a blind mapmaker who trades in secrets, to learn the way into the court beneath the mountain. Vess demands a memory as payment—and chooses one Emrys didn't know they had. POV: Emrys. Emotional beat: the cost of knowledge made literal.

chapters.title: Tam's Empty Chair
chapters.summary: Bram's mother has begun setting a place for a son who sits at the table but casts no shadow and speaks only in borrowed voices. Bram confronts what her bargain actually purchased. POV: Bram. Emotional beat: horror that love was the currency all along.

chapters.title: Down the Smuggler's Spine
chapters.summary: Emrys and Bram travel the forbidden deep roads together, Bram learning the mountains' hidden grammar while Emrys teaches her survival. Their wary alliance begins to soften into trust. POV: alternating. Emotional beat: two exiles—one from society, one from innocence—finding common ground.

chapters.title: The Tollgate of Names
chapters.summary: At the threshold of the Ember Court stands a gate that demands each traveler surrender a true name to pass. Emrys, having none to give, must improvise a deception that costs them blood. POV: Emrys. Emotional beat: terror that their erasure may be the very thing that damns them.

chapters.title: Court of the Quiet Fire
chapters.summary: Inside, the Ember Court glitters with souls kept as heirlooms. Emrys poses as a soul-broker while cataloguing the vaults, glimpsing shelves upon shelves of lives reduced to embers. POV: Emrys. Emotional beat: revulsion and a terrible flicker of recognition.

chapters.title: The Archivist Who Knew Them
chapters.summary: The court's Archivist greets Emrys by a name no living person should know—and offers to sell back the memories Emrys burned away years ago. POV: Emrys. Emotional beat: vertigo between the person they became and the person they paid to forget.

chapters.title: One Memory, Refunded
chapters.summary: Desperate for leverage, Emrys buys back a single memory: the night they called a storm that killed a village, and the god who ordered it. They learn their exile was a sentence they passed on themselves. POV: Emrys. Emotional beat: grief for a self they can never unbecome.

chapters.title: Bram Among the Heirlooms
chapters.summary: Separated from Emrys, Bram wanders the vaults and finds Tam's ember—small, cold, still faintly hers. She steals it, triggering the court's alarms. POV: Bram. Emotional beat: courage born of guilt, finally aimed at repair instead of escape.

chapters.title: The Hunt Beneath the Mountain
chapters.summary: Pursued through galleries of burning names, Emrys and Bram flee toward the surface road—but the solstice is hours away, and the mark on Bram's palm is turning to open flame. POV: alternating. Emotional beat: panic sharpened into partnership.

chapters.title: Vess's Last Map
chapters.summary: They reach Vess, who reveals the court's weakness: it runs on worship, and worship can be redirected. But the ritual requires someone the gods remember—and Emrys is the only soul in Thornfell the old gods ever loved. POV: Vess. Emotional beat: sacrifice offered quietly, without drama.

chapters.title: The Solstice Rises
chapters.summary: At Cinderhollow, the villagers gather at the answered shrines, unknowingly feeding the court's power. The sky above the mountain burns ember-orange as the vessel-rite begins pulling Bram apart. POV: Bram. Emotional beat: terror transfigured into defiance—she refuses to be a door.

chapters.title: Storm-Caller, Remembered
chapters.summary: Emrys climbs the shrine-mountain and does the unthinkable: calls down a storm while speaking their true name aloud, making themselves visible to every god and mortal at once. The court's attention pivots from Bram to them. POV: Emrys. Emotional beat: liberation in self-destruction.

chapters.title: The Vault of Emrys Galloway
chapters.summary: Dragged before the court, Emrys bargains: their entire hoard of erased memories—all the years of self they buried—in exchange for Tam's soul and Bram's freedom. The Archivist accepts with something like pity. POV: Emrys. Emotional beat: the price of survival, paid in full.

chapters.title: Ash and Aftermath
chapters.summary: The court, glutted on Emrys's surrendered past, goes quiet; the shrines cool and the old gods sink back into sleep, unfed and unremembered. Tam wakes whole, casting a shadow again. POV: Bram. Emotional beat: relief shadowed by the question of what Emrys lost.

chapters.title: A Stranger in Their Own Life
chapters.summary: Emrys wakes on the mountainside with no memory of why they climbed it or who they saved. Bram finds them and must decide whether to tell a stranger the story of their own sacrifice. POV: Bram. Emotional beat: the weight of being someone else's memory-keeper.

chapters.title: The Telling
chapters.summary: Bram walks Emrys down the mountain, recounting everything—the storm, the bargain, the name spoken aloud. Emrys cannot feel the truth of it, but chooses to believe her, and chooses to stay near the people who remember them. POV: alternating. Emotional beat: identity rebuilt from testimony rather than memory.

chapters.title: Ember, Kept
chapters.summary: Seasons later, Emrys lives openly in Cinderhollow, powerless but known, keeping a small coal from the dead court in a lantern as a reminder. Bram asks if they regret the trade; Emrys answers that survival was never meant to be free. POV: Emrys. Emotional beat: hard-won peace—the price paid, and worth it.
